WELCOME AT FLUSHING.

label: text
text: Flushing, Nov. 7

label: text
text: Princess Astrid was received with ceremony and greeted with enthusiasm on arrival here on board a Swedish warship on route to Antwerp—Reuter.

label: text
text: (In the presence of the Kings of Sweden, Norway and Denmark) uncles of the bride, the King of Belgium, and a score of other Royal personages and 1,200 guests, the civil marriage of Princess Astrid of Sweden to the heir to the Belgian throne. Prince Leopold, Duke of Brabant took place at Stockholm in the ancient Throne Room by the Burgomaster. The religious ceremony is to take place in Brussels on Nov. 10.

label: paragraph_title
text: COAL STRUGGLE

label: paragraph_title
text: GREAT COST TO THE COUNTRY:

label: text
text: London, Nov. 6.

label: text
text: The steadily increasing number of m era resuming (at present 300,000 working), together with the mild weather, has mitigated the effects of the coal stoppage during the past week, in which unemployment has diminished by 4,000 but nevertheless still exceeds 1,500,000. A disquieting estimate of the cost of the stoppage was given by Mr. Walter Runciman in a speech at the Chamber of Commerce, Liverpool, namely, between £216,000,000 and £270,000,000 of which textile accounted for £26,000,000.

label: text
text: On the other hand capital issues to October 31 totalled £205,000,000, which is £11,000,000 above last year.

label: text
text: Considerable hope attached to the re-opened negotiations owing to the appreciable assimilation of viewpoints of the two sides, although formidable hurdles remain to the negotiated.

label: text
text: It is understood that the miners are asking, firstly, for the coordination of district agreements, which represents a concession since district agreements are thereby recognised; secondly, a guarantee of a minimum wage; and thirdly, a fixed ratio between wages and profits varied according to the number of hours worked. The last-named constitutes a snag since it implies a national agreement which the owners have hitherto opposed.—Reuter.

label: text
text: To-day's resumption of the coal negotiations opened with the Trade Union Congress mediators hopeful and the miners' leaders non-committal.

label: text
text:
The coal owners are reported to be determined not to sign any national document or form of agreement with the Miners' Federation.
Following a Cabinet meeting both owners and miners are expected to meet the Government this afternoon. The negotiations may be continued during the week-end if there is no break down to-day, and in that event the miners' delegate conference will be recalled to London on Armistice Day to conclude an armistice for a settlement. — Reuter.

label: text
text: Although the miners and mine owners have not yet met, and the Government statement is only of the briefest regarding to-day's meetings of the Coal Committee with the owners, and subsequently with the Miners' Executive, Reuter learns that the Government communicated to the latter the rational principles which it is believed the owners may accept. — Reuter.

label: text
text: The coal negotiations have been adjourned till Monday.—Reuter. London, Nov. 6.

label: text
text:
The Cabinet Coal Committee and the mine owners conferred for an hour and three quarters. Then the T.U.C. Mediation Committee and the full Miners' Executive met the Cabinet Committee. Reuter.
The Cabinet met this morning to consider their reply to the proposals put forward yesterday by the miners' leaders. label: paragraph_title
text: FLANDERS POPPIES

label: text
text: EFFORT TỔ RAISE £500,000!

label: text
text: Over 30,000,000 artificial Flanders Poppies made at the workshops where 200 severely disabled ex-Service men are continuously employed on their manufacture are being distributed for sale on Armitice Day in aid of the British Legion Funds, for ex-Service men of all ranks.

label: text
text:
Poppy Day is one of most successful of these charitable efforts held in Britain. Five years ago over £100,000 was raised by sale of these favours, but the figure has been increased substantially enough year since, and last year £395,000 was raised in this way for the fund over which Earl Haig presides.
The aim this year is to raise half a million pounds. The tptal administrative cost of raising these sums does not exceed five per cent. The appeal does not extend to the Dominions, which have their own organisations, but large sums have in past come from some of the other overseas parts of the Empire.
—British Wireless Service.

label: paragraph_title
text: RUGBY'S WONDERS

label: paragraph_title
text: A WIRELESS TELEPHONE:

label: text
text: TALKING ACROSS ATLANTIC

label: paragraph_title
text: Rugby, Nov. 7.

label: text
text: The Dominion delegates made an inspection yesterday of the high power wireless station at Rugby and were deeply impressed by its vital importance to the Empire as a means for the dissemination of general news.

label: text
text: Messages of greeting were sent to Australia by the Australian Premier, the Rt. Hon. S. M. Bruce, to which, within twenty minutes, a reply was received at Rugby by cable.

label: text
text: This served to emphasise the new intimacy which has thus been established between Britain and the Overseas Dominions.

label: text
text: Particular interest was displayed by the visitors in the wireless telephone transmitting apparatus, with which experiments in trans-Atlantic telephony are now proceeding so well that it is hoped to start a regular commercial service within the next couple of months.— British Wireless Service.

label: text
text:
ditions in regard to national coordinating principles. These are considered to represent, in fact, the maximum hopes of the Miners' Federation for preservation of a national status. It is these conditions which the Cabinet merely listened to in the proposals of the miners' leaders and did not, in any way, indicate whether they approved or dissented. After they have examined the proposals they will meet the coal-owners in order to hear the views of the latter.
Too much optimism is not displayed in Government circles: it is agreed that the miners' leaders have made a considerable advance towards the possibility of settlement. It is considered unlikely that all the miners' conditions will prove acceptable, but the proposals will, if is thought, prove a practical basis for negotiations.
Sir Arthur Steel Maitland, Minister of Labour, speaking in Boote last night, said there were two things essential for a settlement. There must be agreement in the different districts. Although the districts came to settlements by themselves, he thought there ought to be certain general or national principles which should be a sort of skeleton embodied in all the different districts so that the different settlements might be comparable with one another.
The coal negotiations continued at Downing Street throughout the afternoon, the Premier with the members of his Cabinet having a long meeting first with the Miners' Executive and afterwards with the Mining Association representatives of the owners.
The extent of the progress made is not announced, but it has been arranged that discussions between the Government and the Miners' Executive will be continued on Monday afternoon. — Reuter.

label: text
text: COLONEL GARIBALDI'S POSITION.

label: text
text: DID NOT BETRAY FRIENDS

label: text
text: Coronel Ricciotti Gurlbaldi has indignantly protested against the accusation that he betrayed his friends.

label: text
text: In an explanation of Lapolla's visit, Garibaldi has offered a semi-official statement to the effect that the former went to France purely for the purpose of taking precautions against entry into Italy of the suspected plotter, Scivoli, against Mussolini's life. Lapolla in the course of his duties approached Garibaldi, who was acquainted with Seivoli.

label: text
text: The statement adds that Lapolla afterwards again met Garibaldi to return him Scivoli's passport, which he had obtained with a view to photographing. — Reuter.

label: text
text: The relations of Colonel Ricciotti Garibaldi, who has hitherto been indentified with the anti-Fascist movement, and the Italian police inspector Lapolla were questioned at the Paris police headquarters. Garibaldi was alleged to have ad

label: text
text: mitted receiving half a million frances from the Italian police through Lapolla. The "Petit Parisien" declared it was now certain that Garibaldi did not hesitate to lend assistance and his name to enterprises against Mussolini, but he had a prior agreement with the Italian police.

label: paragraph_title
text: ABROGATED.

label: paragraph_title
text:
CHINESE TREATY WITH
BELGIUM.

label: text
text:
Peking, Nov. 6.
The Chinese Government has
abrogated the Sino-Belgian Treaty
of 1865.—Reuter.

label: text
text: Peking, Nov. 6.

label: text
text:
The abrogation of the Sino-Belgian Treaty is considered in diplomatic circles as the most important event in China for a considerable time. It is pointed out that the abrogation has abolished Belgium's extraterritorial rights and places. Belgians in the same position as Austrians, Germans and Russians. M. De Warzee, however, is still treating the situation calmly, and is hopeful regarding the treatment of Belgians throughout China.
Foreign diplomats point out that the Waichiaopu's action is a serious breach of treaties as Belgium alone had the right to propose a modification or abrogation, and further that Mr. Wellington Koo, by declining to agree to Belgium's request to submit the matter to The Hague has violated Article 40 of the Protocol signed at Geneva by the Chinese and other Governments, wherein it was agreed to recognise the competence of The Hague Court, instituted in accordance with the Covenant of the League of Nations, and to submit thereto such questions. China's action, therefore, is regarded as flaunting the League.—Reuter.

label: text
text:
Canton, Nov. 6,
The coercive measures again Chinese students in Belgium has provoked indignation in popular circles here. The Nationalist Government has received requests to issue a strong protest against the attitude of the Belgian Government in expelling students for their demonstration favouring negotiation of a new Sino-Belgian Treaty, and all local organisations are planning a mass demonstration on the late Dr. Sun Eat-sen's birthday, November 12.—"Canton Information Bureau," through Reuter.
